items.title: Hope for the Worst of Sinners
items.summary: When it comes to being a candidate for grace, your background has nothing to do with God’s choice. That’s good news.

items.title: Let Goods and Kindred Go
items.summary: You have a possession in heaven that is better, and lasts longer, than anything this world can offer.

items.title: Ammunition Against Anxiety
items.summary: God intends for particular promises to help you fight against particular anxieties.

items.title: Not Nearly Hedonistic Enough
items.summary: The Lord has spoken: It is more blessed to love than to live in luxury! More blessed now, and forever.

items.title: Our Unspeakable Privilege
items.summary: In Jesus Christ we who are born of God have the unspeakable privilege of knowing Yahweh as our Father.

items.title: The Only True Freedom
items.summary: Only Jesus, the Son of God who died and rose for us, can make us truly free.

items.title: Worship in a Lightning Storm
items.summary: Sit down to the feast of joy in Christ and worship the King of Glory. The banquet hall is very large.

items.title: Six Traits of a Forgettable Sermon
items.summary: Rigorous exposition isn’t at odds with engaging preaching. Pastor John encourages pastors to work for creativity when technical, abstract sermons feel easier.

items.title: Do We Need to Go to Church Every Week?
items.summary: Gathering with other Christians is a crucial way to encourage and be encouraged in Christ. But do we really need to gather every week?

items.title: The Joy That Sustained Jesus
items.summary: Jesus endured unspeakable agony at the cross. Pastor John marvels at the force of his love sustained by expectant joy.

items.title: The Barrier to Doctrinal Maturity
items.summary: Is the Bible accessible only to readers with a high IQ? Pastor John reframes biblical maturity as a moral issue centered on our obedience, not our intellect.

items.title: Daily Vigilance for Lifelong Productivity
items.summary: Daily productivity requires often elusive focus and grit. Pastor John offers ten charges to live each day to the glory of God.

items.title: Why Did Jesus Call Her a Dog?
items.summary: Did Jesus demean the Canaanite woman he called a dog? Pastor John explains how Jesus’s test revealed her great faith — and her adoption as one of God’s own.

items.title: Paul’s Detour
items.summary: As we find ourselves discouraged with our circumstances in life, we usually react in one of three ways. We might harden ourselves by saying life is unfair and we should get used to it, we might be overcome by despair, or we might simply believe everything will get better for us soon. The apostle Paul shows us there’s…

items.title: Politics of the Kingdom
items.summary: We sometimes think becoming a Christian is something that has to take a lot of time and effort. As we consider what we believe, it can be easy to feel as if we’re somewhere between “not a believer” and “someone saved by Christ.” But the Bible gives us a different interpretation: we are either strangers to this world…

items.title: The Stories We Live By
items.summary: Get the new book The Stories We Live By this month as our thanks for your gift at gospelinlife.com/give.This video is an excerpt from session 1 of a group study that has also been created to complement the new book. The Stories We Live By Bible Study Guide releases Nov 3rd, but can be pre-ordered today from…

items.title: House of God (Part 4)
items.summary: When we think of what it means to be holy, many of us think of a perfect person who never does anything wrong. And if the apostle Paul says that we are being shaped to be holy, how could we ever live up to such a standard? The Bible, thankfully, gives us a bigger definition of the word. To be holy means to be wholly…

items.title: House of God (Part 3)
items.summary: In the Book of Ephesians, the apostle Paul calls Christians stones of a holy temple “built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets…” But what does it really mean that these figures of the early church are our foundation, and why is it important? By studying the apostles and prophets’ teachings in the Word of…

items.title: House of God (Part 2)
items.summary: One of the biggest questions the Bible answers is, “If human beings have been separated from God, how can we be in his presence again?” The good news is this: from the days of Adam and Eve to our own lives today, God has been working out a plan that allows us to dwell with him once again. The apostle Paul describes…

items.title: Following the Golden Rule
items.summary: As we yield to the Holy Spirit, we become more like Christ.

items.title: God's Response to Sin
items.summary: God can respond to sin in different ways, but His character never changes.

items.title: God's Sovereignty
items.summary: Though we may never fully comprehend God's sovereignty, we can always trust in His goodness.

items.title: When Light Meets Darkness
items.summary: Facing persecution allows us the opportunity to be a witness in a powerful way. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

items.title: An Invaluable Gift
items.summary: Scripture is a life-changing treasure. How can we make it a priority in our daily life? See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

items.title: The Book of Books
items.summary: God's Word gives us direction, strength, and understanding that no other book can offer.

items.title: We Can't Obey on Our Terms
items.summary: True obedience requires complete surrender without any attempt to find a compromise. See omnystudio.com/listener for privacy information.

items.title: A Call to Repentance (2 Kings 24:3)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 24:3, David Platt draws lessons on the importance of repentance, obedience, and urgent evangelism. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: God Alone Is Worthy (2 Kings 23:4)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 23:4, David Platt calls believers to turn from idols and devote their worship to the Lord. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Biblical Repentance (2 Kings 22:11)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 22:11, David Platt highlights the power of Scripture to lead us to genuine repentance. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Selfless Love (2 Kings 20:19)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 20:19, David Platt calls us to genuinely care for the needs of others. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Saved by God (2 Kings 19:19)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 19:19, David Platt reminds us that God saves us for his glory and our good. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Faith Through Trials (2 Kings 18:5–7)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 18:5–7, David Platt encourages us to hold fast to God in faith no matter what we face. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Fear God, Reject Idols (2 Kings 17:33)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Kings 17:33, David Platt urges believers to reject idols and give God their wholehearted devotion. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: No One Is Above God
items.summary: The name El Elyon means “God Most High,” declaring God’s absolute supremacy over everyone and everything. In this final episode of the Names of God series, Costi Hinn explains what it means to live with the perspective that God is sovereign, owns everything, and answers to no one.

items.title: Why Is God Jealous?
items.summary: God’s jealousy is not sinful, insecure, or possessive. It is His holy zeal for His glory and His covenant relationship with His people. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be El Qanna, the jealous God, and why He refuses to share the worship that belongs exclusively to Him.

items.title: God Is Stronger Than Your Circumstances
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explores El Gibbor, the Mighty God, and what this name reveals about the strength, sovereignty, and victory of God. When life feels bigger than you, remember: you don’t have to be strong enough. Your God is.

items.title: The God Who Sees You
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explores the name El Roi—the God who sees me. Through the story of Hagar, we’re reminded that God sees us in our pain, our struggles, and the moments when everyone else overlooks us. But His seeing also means He sees our sin, our motives, and our private lives. El Roi brings both comfort…

items.title: When God Does the Impossible
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn continues the Names of God series by exploring El Shaddai—God Almighty. Through the story of Abraham, we see that our limitations are never a limitation for God. When our strength runs out, His resources never do.
